prompt: A man in his sixties stands at an arrivals gate holding a cardboard name card he no longer needs; a young woman with a duffel bag sees him mid-stride, stops short, drops the bag strap and runs the last ten metres. The camera holds at chest height inside the crowd, then tracks with her through blurred shoulders. Late afternoon light through terminal glass, long reflections on polished floor. Creased travel clothes, scuffed wheels, tape on the sign. Gate announcements and rolling suitcase wheels.
title: Reunion at the Gate
summary: A name card no longer needed: a young woman drops her bag and runs the last ten metres.
why: The prop carries the story: a name card held by someone who clearly does not need it tells you the relationship before anyone moves. The prompt stages three readable states — stop, drop, run — which is what a model can actually animate over eight seconds, and the crowd crossing the foreground hides the joins. Written at chest height with ambient terminal sound so the beat feels observed rather than staged.
